result:
Compiled successfully. I wrote `tests/org/apache/commons/csv/ExtendedBufferedReaderAgentTest.java`, covering:

- Initial state (`getPosition`, `getLineNumber`, `getBytesRead`, `getLastChar` sentinel outside the documented 0–65535 range)
- `read()` single-char and EOF behavior, including `lastChar` tracking
- `read(char[], int, int)` happy path, zero-length, EOF, and out-of-range offset/length
- `readLine()` with LF, CRLF, CR terminators, empty lines, EOF-without-terminator, and line-number increments
- `mark()`/`reset()` round-trip and `reset()` without a prior mark throwing `IOException`
- `close()` followed by `read()` throwing `IOException`
- Byte-tracking constructor variants (disabled, enabled-with-null-charset, enabled-with-charset) verifying `getBytesRead()`
- Position counting characters vs. bytes using a multi-byte UTF-8 character

All assertions trace back to the documented javadoc contract (or well-established `java.io.Reader`/`BufferedReader` base contracts the class overrides without altering), per the restriction against guessing at implementation details.
